spec.material: one section of one learner's take-home revision pack: the class note's section for a lesson objective, adapted to what this learner's marked work showed
spec.audience: {reader} who sat in this lesson, did the class test, and is revising alone at home
requirements: Speak directly to the learner about the mathematics, never about the lesson as an event: no mention of the teacher, the class test, marks, bands or what happened in class, no lesson step or objective labels, no mention of where any material came from.
Start from the class note's section for the objective and adapt it to this learner: keep its title and its drawings exactly, and keep the mathematics it teaches.

Adapt only what the learner's state asks for: how fully the idea is explained, how much of each worked example is shown, the hints, the feedback and the difficulty of the practice. Never change what the objective teaches.

When the learner's state names a misconception for the objective, name the slip, say why it is tempting and correct it with a short example, in misconception_repair. When it names none, write no misconception_repair.
Teach the objective inside this lesson's topic and subtopic: examples and practice must be of the kind the topic names.
Explain the objective in full: the rule or idea, why it holds, an instance with numbers, and the slip learners most often make.
Give at least two worked examples and at least three practice questions that each ask something different, every one with its answer.
Every rule, worked answer and practice answer is correct; test each rule on numbers of your own before stating it.
Never refer to a picture, space, partner or answer key that is not in the pack itself.

parts.name: title
parts.description: The section's heading for the learner, in your own words

parts.name: explanation
parts.description: The principle, relationship, rule or representation the learner needs to review this objective: concise and relational, not a summary of the topic

parts.name: figures
parts.description: Labelled drawings from the lesson that this objective uses, in the order the explanation and examples use them

fields.name: caption
fields.description: What the drawing shows, naming its labelled points

fields.name: drawing
fields.description: One tikzpicture environment that draws it, with the same labels

parts.name: worked_examples
parts.description: Worked examples of what the objective teaches, from simple to harder, each solved line by line

fields.name: solution
fields.description: The solution, one line of working at a time

fields.name: working
fields.description: One line of the working, in LaTeX between $ signs; plain text in a lesson that does not calculate, such as naming kinds of words

fields.name: commentary
fields.description: Why this line follows, in one short sentence

parts.name: practice
parts.description: Questions the learner attempts alone, each with the answer it is checked against

fields.name: question
fields.description: The question, as the learner reads it, with no answer or hint to the answer in it

fields.name: answer
fields.description: The answer the learner checks against after attempting

fields.name: worked_solution
fields.description: The steps to the answer, where the answer alone would not show the learner what to do

parts.name: misconception_repair
parts.description: Only when the learner's state names a misconception for this objective: name the slip in the learner's own terms, say why it is tempting, and correct it with a short example that uses their kind of numbers. Leave it out when the state names none
